mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20d returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median 20d return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months indicates an overheating labor market, which historically precedes either a pause or reversal in rate hikes and supports risk assets, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly above the median baseline return in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60d returns in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the mean 60d return is not significantly below zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average, coincident with a decline in the housing starts index (HOUST), signals a broad-based supply shock, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-mo MA AND HOUST < 12-mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly below zero in triggered months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a simultaneous monetary tightening and inflationary pressure episode, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-mo MA AND CPIAUCSL > 12-mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5d returns are not significantly negative in triggered months (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above the prior 6-month average, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion, which typically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly above zero in triggered months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, while personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) are flat or declining, signals a precautionary savings regime that typically precedes a slowdown in consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo MA AND GDPC1 ≤ 12-mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly below zero in triggered months (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,400,000 units for three consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which historically drags on construction and materials equities and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly below zero in triggered episodes (p > 0.05).
